overview: Two types of white blood cells (agranulocytes) with very different jobs — targeted immune defence versus general clean-up.
genZNote: Lymphocytes: the specialised strike team (B cells and T cells). Monocytes: the general clean-up crew that becomes macrophages.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Mounts specific, adaptive immune responses (antibody production, cell-mediated killing).
aspects.valueB: Differentiates into macrophages/dendritic cells to phagocytose debris and pathogens, and present antigens.

aspects.label: Relative Size
aspects.valueA: Small to medium-sized cell with a large nucleus and little cytoplasm.
aspects.valueB: Largest of all white blood cells, with abundant cytoplasm.

aspects.label: Subtypes
aspects.valueA: B cells, T cells, and natural killer (NK) cells.
aspects.valueB: Differentiates into macrophages (tissue) or dendritic cells.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Monocytes are the largest circulating white blood cell and become macrophages once they migrate into tissue.
overlay.memoryTrick: Lymphocytes = adaptive immunity specialists. Monocytes = become the body's macrophage clean-up crew.
overlay.commonMisconception: Monocytes and macrophages are not entirely separate cell types — a macrophage is simply what a monocyte becomes after it enters tissue.
